messages:
customer_acme: Hey, hitting a regression with the /rerank endpoint. Our TS client returns a different ordering than the raw API response. Looks like scores are correct in the HTTP response but the SDK-sorted candidates come back in the wrong order.

kai (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste the raw response body you got (curl or from network tab) and the SDK call you made? Also which SDK version?

customer_acme: Using @redwood/sdk v0.8.3 (ts). Raw response:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"A","score":"10"},
    {"id":"B","score":"2"},
    {"id":"C","score":"1"}
  ]
}
```
But the client returned ordering B,C,A.

kai (Support): Thanks. That makes me suspect the client is treating scores as strings and doing a lexicographic sort somewhere. Can you also paste the snippet of how you call client.rerank()?

customer_acme: Sure. TS call (simplified):
```
const res = await redwood.rerank({
  query: "find best",
  candidates: [{id: 'A', text: '...'}, {id: 'B', text: '...'}, {id: 'C', text: '...'}]
});
// res.candidates is out of order
```
We didn't do any post-sort. SDK returns it.

maria (SDK Eng): pinging in. Can you share package lock / node version? Also curious if scores are strings in other cases or only when quoted by server.

customer_acme: node 18.16.0, npm lock included. We see server quoting scores for some rerank models (legacy bridge). Most responses are numeric but a subset come as quoted strings.

maria (SDK Eng): Ok thanks — I pulled the v0.8.3 client code. There's a sort helper in packages/rerank/src/index.ts that was added in v0.8.0. It currently does: 
```
// buggy comparator
candidates.sort((a, b) => String(b.score).localeCompare(String(a.score)));
```
LocaleCompare is lexicographic and will order "10" < "2". That explains the B,A swap you saw.

noah (Backend Eng): FWIW, the API sometimes serializes scores as strings to preserve precision for downstream clients, but we expect SDKs to parse numeric fields.

maria (SDK Eng): Thanks @noah. Fix will be to coerce to Number and use numeric comparator:
```
candidates.sort((a,b) => (Number(b.score) || 0) - (Number(a.score) || 0));
```
I'll add tests for quoted numeric scores and for null/missing scores.

kai (Support): For now, quick workaround for the customer: map over res.candidates and parseFloat on score, then sort with a numeric comparator.

customer_acme: Thanks — workaround worked. After parsing and sorting client-side ordering matches API. Appreciate a proper SDK patch.

maria (SDK Eng): Filed PR #2247 with fix + unit tests. Linking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2247. Will cut a patch release after CI.

deploy-bot: CI passed for PR #2247 on main. Releases prepared: v0.8.4 (patch).

maria (SDK Eng): v0.8.4 released with the numeric sort and parsing fix. Changelog: "Fix(rerank): ensure numeric comparison for returned scores when server emits quoted numbers (lexicographic sort bug)".

customer_acme: Confirmed v0.8.4 fixes it for us. Ordering now matches raw HTTP response. Thanks team :thumbsup:

kai (Support): Closing after we get your confirmation. Reopen if anything else pops up.
